data.title: Modi summons telecom secretary over website takedowns, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Government probes intensifying on why fake court orders led to takedowns
  • Telecom secretary to cut short trip to appear in person at Modi's office
  • Telecoms ministry has begun internal inquiry, police seek records
  • Fake orders removed from government website on Saturday

By Aftab Ahmed, Munsif Vengattil and Aditya Kalra

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office summoned the telecommunications secretary on Saturday to explain how officials ordered the takedown of more than 100 websites based on court orders that Reuters revealed were fake, two government sources said.

The intervention from Modi's office signals intensifying scrutiny after Reuters revealed on Wednesday that telecom officials directed internet providers to block 129 illegal betting websites based on fake High Court orders which were emailed to officials by people posing as lawyers.

While online betting is illegal in India, the case has raised concerns that a lack of safeguards in India's content-takedown system could allow falsified court documents to be used to block legitimate websites.

The findings have triggered one criminal investigation by state police against unknown persons for forgery and cheating.

Modi's office summoned Telecom Secretary Amit Agrawal to appear and explain the lapse, cutting short Agrawal's trip to another state, said the two government officials with knowledge of the matter.

Agrawal is the most senior bureaucrat in the telecommunications ministry, which oversees everyone from big telecom operators to internet providers.

"The action taken by the Department of Telecommunications against betting accounts was carried out through the relevant field officers," said one of the people.

Agrawal and his ministry did not respond to Reuters queries, and neither did Modi's office.

Court precedents generated using AI have caused concerns among judges the world over. India's Supreme Court in July set aside a tribunal's orders that relied on non-existent judgments, and a US judge recently disqualified lawyers over use of fabricated legal citations.

On Friday, Reuters reported that the telecoms ministry had initiated an internal investigation into the alleged fraud, while police have sought ministry records as part of a criminal investigation.

The two state court orders Reuters revealed were fake, based on comments from police and the court registry, contained fabricated court logos and seals, ​as well as a fake QR code.

They were for months available publicly on the Department of Telecommunications' website, along with correspondence that showed government officials ordering internet providers to remove the websites.

On Saturday, one of the fake court orders was still accessible on the government's website, while one had been removed.

data.title: Tesla invites select customers to buy Cybercab for personal use
data.description:
Tesla said on Friday it was inviting select customers to buy the Cybercab for personal use, marking a push towards delivering fully designed autonomous vehicles to customers.

  • Tesla posted the announcement on X with an image of the golden butterfly door two-seater, priced at $29,990 with an “Autonomy Subscription” of $299 a month.

  • Chief Executive Elon Musk said in a post on X that the offering would be available nationwide as Tesla receives regulatory approval

  • "The monthly fee is too high," Musk said, adding that it should match the cost of Tesla Full Self Driving and connectivity for other models, which is about $115 per month

  • The EV maker aims to start selling its Cybercab robotaxis to the public by the end of this year, Lars Moravy, Tesla's vice president of vehicle engineering, said last month

  • The Cybercab will work unsupervised in all the same geo locations as the robotaxi, Tesla’s head of artificial intelligence, Ashok Elluswamy, said in a separate X post

  • Tesla launched its unsupervised robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, in June 2025, expanded the offering to Dallas and Houston in April 2026 and rolled it out in Miami in July 2026

data.title: Twenty One Capital CEO Says ‘A Balance Sheet Is Not A Business’ After $1 Billion Bitcoin-Driven Gain
data.description:
Key points:
  • Twenty One Capital CEO Raphael Zagury also said he did not want the company’s success to rest on predicting markets.
  • Zagury also said the company could buy back its own stock, but no buyback has been announced yet.
  • The company reported net income of $1.087 billion for its third quarter which ended on September 30.

Twenty One Capital (XXI) CEO Raphael Zagury told shareholders that the company needed to build a real business around its Bitcoin (BTC) holdings, adding that 'Bitcoin remains our benchmark.' The company’s profit from Bitcoin alone stood at a little over $1 billion in its third quarter.

In a shareholder letter, Zagury explained that “A balance sheet is not a business. It is our starting point.” The company reported net income of $1.087 billion for the quarter that ended on September 30. Zagury said that result was “primarily driven by a $1.093 billion fair-value gain” on its Bitcoin, “rather than operating cash flow.”

“We welcome Bitcoin’s appreciation. But gains from an asset we own are not the same as earnings from businesses we operate,” he wrote, adding that, “Building the latter is our job.”

XXI stock was down over 1% during overnight trading. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around XXI remained in the ‘bullish’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘normal’ from ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Bitcoin As The Benchmark

Twenty One ended the September quarter with 43,514 BTC, valued at about $83,700 per coin, and $102.8 million in cash. It had $486.5 million in convertible notes outstanding, secured by about 16,116 BTC. Zagury said Bitcoin was the bar any new investment had to clear.

Any capital the company deployed “should justify the risk, complexity, and opportunity cost of not simply owning more Bitcoin,” he wrote. The company was looking at deals in mining, lending and energy, according to the letter. Zagury said it has already walked away from some of them and expected to walk away from more.

Bitcoin’s price was trading at $67,094, down over 2% in the last 24 hours. On Stocktwits, Bitcoin was one of the top trending tickers among cryptocurrencies at the time of writing.

Retail sentiment around BTCnearly 70% remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

Buybacks On The Table

Zagury also said the company could buy back its own stock. “When our shares trade below the value of the assets attributable to them, repurchases deserve serious consideration,” he wrote, adding that any repurchase would be subject to liquidity, approvals and applicable restrictions.

No buyback has been announced. The letter lists repurchasing shares alongside buying Bitcoin, acquiring businesses and preserving liquidity as competing uses of the company’s capital.

Zagury said he did not want the company’s success to rest on predicting markets. “I would rather build one that can endure when we are wrong, take advantage of opportunities when they appear, and continue creating value through different market environments,” the CEO added.

XXI’s share price has been down over 43% so far this year and nearly 70% in the last 12 months.

data.title: Sammaan Capital Q2 Results: Profit edges up to ₹312 crore, net interest income turns negative
data.description:
Sammaan Capital, on Saturday, November 14, reported a 1.3% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit at ₹312.34 crore for the September quarter from ₹308.47 crore in the year-ago period.

However, the company’s net interest income (NII) or core income turned into a loss of ₹138.06 crore in Q2FY27, against a profit of ₹163.02 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. This is because interest costs of ₹1,299.32 crore exceeded interest income of ₹1,161.26 crore during the quarter.

On a sequential basis, net profit rose 28.4% from ₹243.30 crore in Q1 FY27. Profit before tax increased to ₹424.57 crore from ₹326.01 crore in the previous quarter, while total income rose 10% quarter-on-quarter to ₹1,850.85 crore.

Revenue from operations stood at ₹1,849.97 crore, down from ₹2,250.60 crore in Q2FY26. The year-on-year decline was partly offset by higher gains on fair value changes, which increased to ₹648.11 crore from ₹291.64 crore a year ago.

Gains on derecognition of financial instruments, meanwhile, declined sharply to ₹7.19 crore from ₹468.81 crore.

The company’s assets under management (AUM) stood at ₹59,188 crore as of September 30, up 5% from ₹56,239 crore at the end of the previous quarter. Disbursements rose 62% sequentially to ₹6,278 crore, compared with ₹3,875 crore in Q1FY27. The company disbursed around 30,700 loans during the quarter.

Asset quality improved during the quarter, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 0.15% from 0.21% in Q1 FY27, while net non-performing assets (NNPA) fell to 0.11% from 0.15%. The company reported a blended cumulative collection efficiency of 99.6%.

Sammaan Capital’s capital adequacy ratio stood at 20%, while its net worth was ₹19,445 crore as of September 30, excluding the ₹906 crore received from the first tranche of warrant conversion completed on October 30.

The company also expanded its branch network to 245 branches across 20 states, from 217 branches in the previous quarter. It is targeting 270 branches by the end of FY27.

For the first half of FY27, consolidated profit after tax stood at ₹555.64 crore, compared with ₹642.77 crore in the year-ago period.

Shares of Sammaan Capital ended 0.2% higher at ₹137.80 on Friday, ahead of the September quarter results announcement. The stock has gained almost 4% since January this year.

data.title: India's biggest small-cap mutual fund adds 8 stocks, exits 4 in October 2026; ITC tops fresh buys; expense ratio rises
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- India's biggest active small-cap mutual fund by assets under management (AUM), Nippon India Small Cap Fund, managed Rs.76,903 crore as of October 2026. The fund added eight new stocks and completely exited four others, while also reshuffling its existing holdings.

The fund has 260 stocks in its portfolio. The fresh additions include large-cap stocks such as ITC and Bank of Baroda. Here's what investors need to know about the changes in the fund's portfolio.

The fund added eight new stocks to its portfolio in October. ITC topped the list with 2.15 crore shares, followed by Bank of Baroda, with around 82.21 lakh shares.

Other notable additions included Aequs, with 36.38 lakh shares, and Sahajanand Medical Technologies, with 14.37 lakh shares.

Nippon India Small Cap Fund completely exited four stocks in October. These included Fineotex Chemical, Jio Financial Services, Vedant Fashions, and Asian Paints.

Apart from fresh purchases and complete exits, the fund also adjusted its existing stock positions in October.

The fund increased its holdings in 21 stocks. These included Swiggy, Tata Steel and Kotak Mahindra Bank, with the number of shares added in each at 50 lakh.

On the other hand, the fund reduced its holdings in 11 stocks. State Bank of India, Allied Blenders and Distillers, and UTI Asset Management Company were among the stocks where its exposure declined.

As per the October 2026 factsheet, HDFC Bank was the fund's largest holding, accounting for 2.02% of net assets. It recorded an increase in weightage of 0.27 percentage points. Meanwhile, TD Power Systems and Apar Industries saw the biggest reductions of 0.09 percentage points each.

According to the fund factsheet, Nippon India Small Cap Fund's expense ratio increased marginally in October from September 2026.

For the regular plan, the expense ratio rose from 1.32% to 1.33%. For the direct plan, it increased from 0.60% to 0.61%.

data.title: 'Don't rush to replace Jensen Huang': Nvidia investors urge board to keep comeback option open
data.description:
Two prominent Nvidia investors have urged the company's board to take a measured approach to deciding its future leadership, warning against rushing to appoint a successor to Jensen Huang and asking directors to keep open the possibility of his return as chief executive.

In a letter addressed to the Nvidia board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital, and Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer of Atreides Management, said shareholders deserved a deliberate process as the company navigates the uncertainty surrounding Huang's departure.

Gerstner shared the letter on X on Saturday, November 14, saying it outlined the minimum standards the board owed shareholders as it managed the situation.

Brad Gerstner
@altcap

This letter was sent to the Nvidia Board today which we believe outlines the minimum acceptable standards the Board owes shareholders as it manages this difficult situation. Onward. ???? https://t.co/fIsyXVQ5tR

Nov 13, 2026

The investors said Huang's long record of leadership and the uncertainty surrounding recent events made it important for the board to avoid a rushed decision. They added that Nvidia could continue to be led by interim chief executive Colette Kress and her team while directors took time to assess the situation.

The letter also made clear that the board would retain the right to decide against bringing Huang back if, after all the facts were known, it concluded that his return was not in shareholders' best interests. However, the investors argued that the company's founder and long-time leader deserved a fair and deliberate process before being replaced.

Calls grow for Jensen Huang's return

The letter adds to growing calls from some Nvidia shareholders, employees and industry figures for Huang to return following his sudden exit.

Elon Musk had earlier backed a petition seeking Huang's reinstatement, saying he was signing it in response to a post by a Tesla Superintelligence engineer urging Nvidia employees to stand up for the company's leadership.

Separately, an internal employee suggestion-box post calling for the board to consider employee sentiment drew more than 1,600 comments, most of them supporting Huang's return, according to a Wired report. The internal post was submitted before Huang's resignation and should be distinguished from the petition Musk referred to.

Meanwhile, the Financial Times reported that Nvidia's board had approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a possible successor. Haas previously spent seven years at Nvidia, where he held senior roles, including vice president and general manager of computing products. The report said he was among several potential candidates; there was no confirmation that he had been offered the position.

Why did Jensen Huang leave Nvidia?

Nvidia announced on November 12 that Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member with immediate effect. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named interim CEO, while the board began searching for a permanent successor.

The announcement followed reports about Huang's personal relationships and allegations involving Alice Huang, a Singapore-based businesswoman whom US authorities reportedly suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence. Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful, but Nvidia's official announcement did not specify a reason for his departure.

The developments had prompted scrutiny of the company's leadership and a board-level review. Nvidia said its independent directors had initiated an investigation, adding that the board had no reason to believe that US national security or the company's confidential information had been compromised. Huang has said he supports the review and is cooperating.

The board has yet to announce a permanent successor or clarify whether Huang could return to the company.

data.title: Rs.150 Dividend Alert! Record date next week of Jockey firm for biggest payout declared in Q2 - check key dates, history
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Page Industries, the listed innerwear and athleisure manufacturer, has announced its second interim dividend for FY27, making it the only company so far to declare a three-digit interim dividend during the September quarter. The company has declared a payout of Rs.150 per equity share, the largest among the interim dividends announced during Q2 FY27, with the record date scheduled for next week.

The dividend announcement comes alongside the company's September-quarter results, which showed a 4% increase in net profit. However, the stock has remained under pressure, declining 21% over the past year. Investors will therefore be tracking both the upcoming dividend record date and the company's financial performance.

The company's board of directors considered and approved the second interim dividend for FY27.

"The Board of Directors of the Company at their meeting held today (i.e., 12 November 2026) has declared the 2nd Interim Dividend for the financial year 2026-27 for an amount of Rs.150/- per equity share," read the BSE filing released earlier in the day.

The Rs.150 per-share payout is the largest interim dividend announced so far during the September quarter.

The board has fixed Wednesday, November 18, 2026, as the record date to determine shareholders' eligibility for the dividend. This effectively makes Tuesday, November 17, the last date for investors to qualify for the corporate action.

"The record date fixed for the payment of interim dividend is 18 November 2026. The date fixed for payment of dividend is on or before 11 December 2026," read the BSE filing.

The company has stated that the dividend payment will be completed on or before December 11, 2026.

Since 2024, Page Industries Ltd. has distributed Rs.1,800 per share through ten interim dividends.

In FY2024-25, the company announced four payouts aggregating Rs.900 per share. These included Rs.300 in August 2024, followed by Rs.250 in November 2024, Rs.150 in February 2025 and Rs.200 in May 2025.

For FY2025-26, Page Industries distributed another four interim dividends totalling Rs.550 per share. The company paid Rs.150 in August 2025, Rs.125 in November 2025, Rs.125 in February 2026 and Rs.150 in May 2026.

Continuing into FY2026-27, the company declared a first interim dividend of Rs.200 in August 2026 and a second interim dividend of Rs.150 in November 2026, with the record date set for November 18, 2026. This takes the dividend declared for the current financial year to Rs.350 per share so far.

Alongside Page Industries' Rs.150 payout, several major Indian companies announced notable interim dividends during the Q2 FY27 earnings season.

Sanofi India led the group with an interim dividend of Rs.75 per share, followed by IT major Infosys, which announced a payout of Rs.26 per share.

In the industrial and specialty chemicals sectors, Ingersoll-Rand India declared Rs.20 per share, while Galaxy Surfactants approved a dividend of Rs.18 per share. Great Eastern Shipping Company rounded out the notable double-digit dividend announcements with an interim payout of Rs.14.40 per share.

Stock price trend

Page Industries shares have remained under pressure in recent periods. The stock declined 13% in one week, 16% in one month and 21% over the past year.

The shares ended 2% lower at Rs.31,399.65 apiece on the BSE on Friday. The stock had touched its 52-week high of Rs.43,823.90 in July 2026 and its 52-week low of Rs.29,800 in March 2026.

Page Industries reported an 11.5% year-on-year increase in net revenue to Rs.1,439 crore during the September quarter. The Jockey licensee also recorded a 5.5% increase in sales volume.

However, profitability growth remained relatively modest amid elevated raw material costs.

The Bengaluru-based apparel manufacturer reported a 7.4% annual increase in EBITDA to Rs.300 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 20.8%. Net profit rose 4% to Rs.202.5 crore, while net total expenses increased 15% to Rs.1,131 crore.

For the first half of FY27, Page Industries reported a 9.7% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs.2,860 crore, while sales volume grew 5.6% to 121.7 million pieces.

Commenting on the results, V.S. Ganesh, Managing Director of Page Industries, said the company delivered double-digit revenue growth in Q2 FY27, supported by healthy volume growth, premiumisation and a strong consumer response to new product launches. He acknowledged that raw material costs remained elevated but said profitability had stayed within the company's planned range.

He added that positive demand trends, strong brand momentum, an encouraging pipeline of new product ranges and ongoing operational efficiency initiatives would support the company's growth outlook.

Brokerage views on Page Industries remain important for investors assessing the stock's prospects after its recent decline and the latest quarterly performance. HSBC has retained a positive view on the company, although it has reduced its target price following weaker-than-expected volume growth.

HSBC maintained its Buy rating on Page Industries but cut its target price to Rs.43,870 per share, implying an upside of approximately 40% from the previous close.

The brokerage highlighted that Page Industries' volume growth slowed to 5.5% in Q2 FY27, significantly below its estimate of 10%. However, it attributed part of the weakness to the shift in the festive calendar. Despite the earnings miss, Page Industries has retained its guidance for double-digit volume growth in FY27. HSBC said achieving this target would require volume growth of approximately 14% in the second half of the financial year.

The brokerage marginally reduced its earnings per share (EPS) estimates for FY27-FY29 by 1-3% and trimmed the valuation multiple assigned to the stock to 48 times earnings.

data.title: Hungary recovers $20 million cash in probe of Orban minister
data.description:
Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million in cash, some buried in forests or hidden in farm buildings and warehouses, in a bribery probe into Miklos Sesztak, a minister under former right-wing leader Viktor Orban.

Prime Minister Peter Magyar ousted nationalist Orban after 16 years in power in an April election, pledging to mend ties with the European Union, marred by years of conflict under Orban, and to launch a sweeping anti-corruption drive into allegations of graft.

Two former ministers from Orban's government and former central bank chief Gyorgy Matolcsy are ​under arrest over graft accusations in separate investigations. They have denied wrongdoing.

Authorities have also detained Orban's brother in a people-smuggling case, which the former leader had dismissed as an act of political revenge.

The clampdown is part of an anti-graft drive the centre-right Magyar has dubbed "Operation Purgatory", considered "very important" by 70% of respondents in a survey by the Median pollster released on news website HVG this week.

"During the searches, investigators found large amounts of cash buried in forests, hidden in farm buildings, warehouses and a residential property, and stored in a high-value safe in a secluded location," the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office said late on Friday.

The cash — 5.07 billion forints ($15.33 million), €2.66 million ($2.93 million) and $1.26 million — took a dozen State Treasury workers eight hours to tot up using five banknote counters, said Finance Minister Andras Karman.

Sesztak, who was Orban's development minister between 2014 and 2018, has denied wrongdoing. His lawyer, Gabor Papp, did not respond to an emailed request for comment on the recovery office's statement.

Magyar said the recovered cash signalled the end of what he described as a "mafia" led by Orban's right-wing Fidesz party and his Christian Democrat allies during Orban's 16-year rule.

Gabor Torok, a political scientist, said images of the large piles of cash were so vivid that they likely spelled doom for Fidesz, whose public support halved to just 16% of voters by November from levels before the vote, a Median survey showed.

data.title: China, US discuss tariffs, farm trade at first trade council meeting
data.description:
China and the United States held their first trade council meeting under a bilateral economic and trade consultation mechanism via video link on Friday, China's commerce ministry said on Saturday.

The two sides held "candid, in-depth and constructive discussions" on implementing outcomes from previous trade consultations, including tariffs, a reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement involving $30 billion on each side, agricultural trade and other issues of note, the ministry said.

Both sides will continue to use the council to address trade concerns, expand cooperation and reduce outstanding issues, it added.

data.title: Rocket Lab Hits 100 Electron Launches, Fastest Commercial Rocket to Reach the Milestone
data.description:
LONG BEACH, Calif., Nov. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation , a global leader in launch services and space systems, today announced mission success for its 100th Electron launch, setting a new record for reaching 100 launches faster than any other commercially developed rocket.

“The Mountain God Rises” mission launched from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand at 6:30 p.m. on November 14, 2026, deploying the YAMATSUMI-II synthetic aperture radar (SAR) Earth-imaging satellite to a 575km low Earth orbit for the Institute for Q-shu Pioneers of Space, Inc. (iQPS). This mission marks Rocket Lab’s 11th Electron launch for iQPS with 100% mission success since 2023. iQPS has booked seven more dedicated Electron launches through 2030 to complete its satellite constellation.

Reaching 100 launches in under a decade is a major milestone for commercial spaceflight. What started as a vision to open up access to space with the world’s first carbon-composite rocket has grown into an unmatched launch cadence across the small-launch industry.

Rocket Lab founder and CEO, Sir Peter Beck, says: “Few rockets reach 100 launches in their total operational lifetime. Not only has Electron now reached 100 launches, but it reached the milestone faster than any other commercially developed rocket. That record pace comes down to the relentless dedication of the Rocket Lab team, and I want to congratulate everyone behind Electron. This is the team that pioneered 3D-printed rocket engines, built the world’s first carbon-composite orbital rocket, launched back-to-back from two hemispheres, and shattered responsive space records along the way, putting Electron in a league of its own. To our customers who have trusted us with their spacecraft, many of them across multiple launches, thank you. The next 100 Electrons are already booked so we’re only accelerating from here.”

Since its first launch in 2017, Electron has deployed hundreds of satellites for commercial constellation operators, national security agencies, and scientific institutions from launch pads in New Zealand and Virginia. Backed by vertically integrated manufacturing and a packed manifest extending well into the next decade, Electron continues to deliver access to orbit while laying the operational foundation for Rocket Lab’s next medium-lift rocket, Neutron.

Rocket Lab is an end-to-end space company delivering rockets, satellites, and spacecraft components for commercial, government, and defense missions. Rocket Lab’s satellites and components have powered more than 1,700 missions in Earth orbit, as well as deep-space exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Learn more at www.rocketlabcorp.com.

data.title: ICICI Bank credit card alert: 6 important changes to be introduced starting from 25 November; check affected cards
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Are you an ICICI Bank credit card holder? If that is the case, then you should be prepared for several changes in how you use your credit card. These changes will be introduced over the next few weeks and will include revised charges and the withdrawal of complimentary benefits scheduled between 25 November and 15 December 2026.

Do note that the new changes will impact different credit card categories at India's second-largest private sector bank, including premium, retail, business, and corporate variants.

The objective of these changes is to improve efficiency and streamline the customer usage and service experience for day-to-day users. Furthermore, while some customers will pay more for card replacement and 'priority pass' services, others will lose complimentary insurance protection and similar movie-related benefits.

Keeping this in mind, here are six key changes that will be implemented over the next few weeks, along with effective dates, possible implications, and the cards that will be impacted.

The first two changes will take effect on 25 November, i.e., in about 10 days. This will be followed by two revisions on 11 December. Finally, the remaining four benefit withdrawals will come into force on 15 December.

The complete details of the upcoming changes are discussed below:

The changes that are going to be introduced from December 15, require particular focus from eligible customers holding premium and co-branded credit cards, as they involve the withdrawal of benefits that may have initially impacted their choice of the card.

ICICI Bank is going to discontinue complimentary air accident and related insurance coverage on Emeralde Private Metal, Times Black, Emeralde Private, Emeralde, Diamant, Sapphiro and Rubyx cards.

Furthermore, it is essential to note that the cancellation for any reason (CFAR) cover is also going to be withdrawn from Emeralde Private Metal, Times Black, Emeralde and Emeralde Private cards. Not only this, separately, Parakram and Parakaram Select cardholders are going to lose their complimentary personal and air accident insurance coverage.

The banking institution is also going to discontinue the complimentary INOX benefit on 9 specified card variants. This will include Coral, Rubyx, Expressions and MakeMyTrip cards.

Therefore, for all eligible customers who consistently use these perks, features, and associated benefits, the upcoming changes may affect the overall value they receive from their credit cards. The higher replacement expenses and new 'priority pass' fee also mean that routine card-related services and day-to-day usage may become more expensive, depending on the kind of card an individual opts for and the associated terms and conditions.

In summary, it can be concluded that credit card users should carefully review the revised terms, conditions, and applicable rules for their specific variants before the respective effective dates, and those who are dependent on complimentary insurance may also need to analyse and assess whether they may require separate coverage rather than assuming that the existing card-linked protection is going to continue, and that any changes are only going to impact the new and upcoming users.

To eliminate such discrepancies and doubts, it is prudent to go through the latest developments and terms and conditions from official sources so that credit card spending, monthly budget and personal finance planning can be done accordingly.

data.title: Metals in the Age of AI — Game-changer or hyperscale hype?: Andy Home
data.description:
By Andy Home

Artificial intelligence may operate in the cloud, but its metallic roots lie in the earth.

Data centers wouldn't exist without a wide spectrum of metals, from galvanised-steel housing and copper wiring to rare earth magnets driving the servers. AI data centers are even more metals-intensive than traditional facilities. They are physically bigger, contain more computing hardware and use more power.

Investors have leaned into AI's metallic backbone.

Copper rode the AI investment wave to all-time highs earlier this year before becoming collateral damage in the recent technology-stock rout.

Tin , which has leapt from the Bronze Age to the AI Age via circuit boards, has been similarly rocked by broader tech turbulence.

But is AI demand for metals really the promised game-changer, or is it hyperscaled hype?

As with any new technology, there's a bit of both in the mix.

METALS TO (ARTIFICIAL) MIND

Data centers consume 60 to 75 metric tons of metals per megawatt (MW), according to a white paper by the World Economic Forum (WEF).

To put that into context, standard data centers use 5 to 10 MW of power, while AI hyperscaler facilities exceed 100 MW, according to the International Energy Agency. Hyperscalers are building the fastest, propelled by US-China competition for AI dominance.

Just about every metal you can name, and a few you probably can't, is deployed in the labyrinth of servers, chips, storage, networks, electrical systems, cooling systems and backup-power facilities.

Aluminium, copper and steel are everywhere in the building. More exotic elements such as gold, silver, cobalt and rare earths are concentrated in the core computing hardware. And backup power is currently a battleground of competing technologies, with lithium, lead and nickel-zinc batteries all fighting for market share.

But in terms of market impact, the three metallic standouts are gallium, germanium and tin. Data center demand will account for 6.0%, 2.4% and 1.2%, respectively, of global annual usage in 2035, according to the WEF report.

Gallium and germanium are tiny markets, and both are used in minute quantities, but they have an exponential impact on semiconductor performance.

China, the dominant producer of both metals, has restricted exports, which is why everyone else is scrambling to find alternative sources of two metals that are literally powering the global AI race.

Tin is less exotic and also remains a small market by base-metal standards, with annual consumption of just over 400,000 tons.

But since the phase-out of lead, tin has become the dominant material for soldering circuit boards. The more complex the ​data center architecture, the more tin it needs to bind everything together.

Copper comes in a distant fourth in the demand-impact table, with data centers accounting for less than 0.9% of global usage in 2035.

Moreover, data centers are likely to start using less copper and other metal as structural designs improve and operating processes become more efficient. Wood Mackenzie expects both copper and aluminium usage to peak in the early 2030s before declining over the rest of the decade.

Who knows, AI itself may be the lead engineer in this technical evolution.

BEYOND THE SERVER ROOM

Copper bulls shouldn't be too disheartened, though. The WEF estimates for data center metals usage stop at the door of the building, excluding the metals needed to provide the power that keeps the whole thing humming away in the clouds.

"The biggest metals story lies outside the facility itself" in the form of transmission lines, substations and energy infrastructure, according to Shashank Sriram, senior research analyst at consultancy Wood Mackenzie, speaking to DataCentre Magazine.

Connecting data centers to the grid or building co-located power plants requires significant volumes of copper, aluminium and zinc for galvanising steel towers and poles.

If power connectivity is included in the equation, actual demand for both copper and aluminium is three or four times the projections based solely on the physical facilities, Wood Mackenzie estimates.

And if data centers draw power from renewable sources such as solar and wind, the demand impact is magnified because these are also highly metal-intensive technologies.

Wood Mackenzie projects power-capacity additions for data centers to rise from 15-20 gigawatts (GW) a year today to 30-33 GW in the early 2030s.

This is where the AI investment meme melds with the existing electrification-of-everything theme. From a market perspective, the two are self-reinforcing bull narratives that are tricky to separate into component drivers.

RAGE AGAINST THE MACHINES

Everything, of course, depends on how many AI data centers are actually built in the next few years, which is where some of the hype comes in.

There are many estimates, all expressed in eye-watering trillions of dollars of investment.

However, many of the new megawatts of announced AI ​computing capacity can more accurately be described as "bragawatts", according to a study by the Oxford Smith School and financial broker Marex Group (8UU.F).

While media and markets price in a rapid, ⁠exponential ramp-up in AI infrastructure, the study says the true outcome is likely to be "a roll-out that is delayed, lumpy, and constrained by physical realities."

The single biggest bottleneck is grid connectivity. A data center can be built in 18 to 24 months, but the ​average US waiting time for a grid connection was four years between 2018 and 2023, the study found.

Compounding the physical hurdles is the growing political backlash against AI.

The Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections on November 3 included gubernatorial wins in Texas and Georgia, where Democrats campaigned in part on a moratorium on new data centers. The incoming Democrats are planning to unleash a flood of new legislation targeting AI systems and data center development when they take control of the US Congress in January.

And it's not just the US where public opinion is turning against the machines.

Protesters broke into the construction site of a Microsoft ​data center in Amsterdam last week, part of coordinated protests across 16 countries under the "Stop Dirty Data Centres" banner.

Politicians are coming under increasing pressure to rein in what many see as the reckless build-out of a technology with unmatched potential to change the world in both good and bad ways.

Anthropic's warning in its IPO prospectus that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" doesn't really help the industry's cause.

POLICY CONTROLS

Government policy is likely to be as important as grid connection times in setting the pace of AI data center construction.

There's an analogy with the electric vehicle (EV) narrative that so excited battery-metal markets a few years ago.

The road to a fossil-fuel-free future has turned out to be a bumpy one, in part due to changeable government subsidy schemes.

The most glaring example is in the US, where President Donald Trump has rolled back his predecessor Joe Biden's subsidies for battery vehicles.

The result has been a collapse in EV sales in the world's second-largest automotive market. Sales in the first 10 months of this year were down 21% from the same period of 2025, according to consultancy Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.

The AI metals revolution could turn out to be just as much a stop-start affair.

But another lesson can also be drawn from the EV sector.

The global roll-out of battery-powered vehicles may not have lived up to its early hype, but it hasn't stopped. Despite plunging sales in the US, global sales were still up 5% year-on-year in January to October.

In other words, governments can restrain growth of a new technology but they can't stop broader adoption.

HERE COME THE ROBOTS

Moreover, building AI's digital infrastructure is only the first part of this latest metals story.

"If digital AI is the brain of the next economy, embodied AI is the beginning of its body," according to Frank Nikolic, research principal for base and precious metals at CRU.

That means "machines that can sense, decide and act in the physical world, widening the addressable market from information work to real-world labour."

The robots are coming, and they are also built with metal.

Early deployment remains selective, CRU noted, but for some industrial functions such as logistics, sorting and inspections, embodied AI has already moved out of the laboratory and is being piloted in real-world environments.

"For commodity markets, the crucial point is not the novelty of the technology itself, but the fact that AI is moving from experimentation toward large-scale deployment and that needs metals and materials," according to Nikolic.

If you're starting to worry we're entering the realm of science fiction, specifically the Terminator films with their eponymous liquid-metal, shape-shifting humanoids, you may have good cause. Researchers are already working on soft robots, which can both handle delicate items, such as eggs, and change shape.

Much of the work centers on room-temperature liquid metals, which make soft robots "extremely deformable with higher degrees of freedom while navigating inside narrow and constrained spaces," according to researchers at China's Shenzhen University, writing for ScienceDirect.

Designers at Carnegie Mellon University in Pennsylvania unveiled a "proof of concept" nano liquid-metal robot in 2023 and, with a nice nod to the Terminator franchise, made it melt through the bars of an enclosed cage.

The metal they used was gallium.

It looks like we have a clear metals winner in the Age of AI.

(The opinions expressed here are those of Andy Home, a columnist for Reuters.)
